memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites set out from Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians, who were burying all their firstborn, whom the Lord had struck down among them; for the Lord had brought judgment on their gods. - Num 33:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The journey began the day after the Passover — the night God's judgment passed over every home covered by the blood of the lamb. Now Israel marched out "defiantly," or boldly, in full view of the Egyptians. A people who had been slaves for four hundred years walked out with their heads held high, redeemed by the power of God. What a transformation: from bondage to boldness in a single night.

Notice the detail that the Lord "had brought judgment on their gods." This was not merely Israel escaping Egypt; it was God demonstrating His supremacy over every false god the Egyptians trusted. The idols could not save. Only the living God could redeem.

This whole scene points forward to something greater. The Passover lamb, whose blood shielded Israel from judgment, was a picture of Jesus, the Lamb of God, whose blood shields us from the judgment our sin deserves (1 Cor 5:7). Just as Israel walked out of slavery the morning after the Passover, we walk out of the bondage of sin because of Christ, our Passover Lamb, who was sacrificed for us.

If you belong to Jesus, you are no longer a slave. You have been redeemed, set free, and given a new dignity as a child of God. You can walk boldly, not in your own strength, but because of what the Lamb has done. The chains are broken. March out with your head held high.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you live as a redeemed person, set free, or still like a slave to old fears?
2. How does seeing Jesus as your Passover Lamb deepen your gratitude?
3. What "bondage" do you need to walk out of in the freedom Christ gives?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, my Passover Lamb, thank You for redeeming me from slavery to sin. Help me to walk in the freedom and dignity You have won for me. Amen.
